authorProfile.shortBio: DJ is a software engineer, writer and podcaster based in Adelaide, Australia, and the creator of How-To-Use-AI.com and Useful Stash. He builds software, automation and cloud infrastructure, likes evidence and strong opinions held loosely, and always asks “but does this actually fucking work?” before getting too excited.
authorProfile.bio:
DJ is an Australian software engineer, technologist, writer, podcaster, builder, and incurable investigator of things that look interesting enough to ruin an otherwise perfectly good evening.

Based in Adelaide, he has spent much of his career working with software engineering, cloud infrastructure, automation, systems integration, security, monitoring, and the sort of technical problems where somebody eventually says, “Surely there’s an easier way to do this,” shortly before discovering there absolutely is not.

His background in technology predates the current AI boom by quite a bit. Machine learning, prediction systems, automation, computer vision, recommendation engines, and intelligent monitoring were already part of the landscape long before ChatGPT turned artificial intelligence into something everyone suddenly had an opinion about. That shift sparked a much broader obsession: not simply with what AI can do, but with what is real, what is useful, what is exaggerated, what is dangerous, what is genuinely transformative, and what is just another company attaching the letters “AI” to something and hoping nobody asks too many questions.

That curiosity became **How-To-Use-AI.com**, a multi-book series designed to make artificial intelligence understandable and genuinely useful to ordinary people, professionals, businesses, and eventually technical builders. The goal is not to preach that AI will save the world, destroy civilisation, replace everybody’s job, or turn humanity into batteries for a machine empire. There is already plenty of that shit on the internet. The goal is to give people enough knowledge, practical experience, evidence, competing viewpoints, and healthy scepticism to make up their own minds.

DJ also created **Useful Stash**, a technology publication built around a fairly simple philosophy: if something is useful, stash it. It covers software engineering, AI, automation, cloud infrastructure, tools, scripts, experiments, open-source projects, and lessons learned while actually building things rather than merely talking about them.

Outside conventional technology, DJ co-hosts **Sisters With Mirrors**, a weekly podcast exploring spirituality, psychology, consciousness, astrology, tarot, aliens, reincarnation, unusual experiences, and the enormous category of questions humanity has been arguing about since somebody first looked at the night sky and thought, “What the fuck is all that?”

That combination probably explains his general approach to life. DJ is comfortable being deeply technical without believing that everything worth discussing can be reduced to a Jira ticket. He likes evidence but also likes questions. He distrusts hype, dislikes intellectual gatekeeping, changes his mind when better information appears, and has very little patience for pretending certainty where none exists.

He is particularly interested in what happens when technology stops being a novelty and becomes infrastructure: when AI becomes part of everyday work, when automation quietly changes professions, when privacy collides with convenience, when software starts making decisions, and when tools become powerful enough that understanding their limitations matters just as much as understanding their features.

Most of his projects begin with some variation of, “I wonder if I could build that,” and frequently end several hours later with terminals everywhere, seventeen browser tabs, an architectural diagram nobody asked for, and another idea he absolutely did not need.

He considers this normal.

books.title: AI for Normal People
books.description: Understanding Artificial Intelligence Without the Hype

dedication.text:
For Johnny,

who has endured more midnight conversations about AI, technology, and whatever else my ADHD brain has decided is fascinating that night than any husband reasonably should.

You listen while I excitedly explain one more idea when we should both be asleep, knowing full well that “one more thing” is never actually one more thing.

And somehow, without fail, you still love me every day.

This book is for you.

epigraph.quote: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.
epigraph.author: Arthur C. Clarke

summary: You've already been using AI in your maps, your inbox, your bank and your streaming queue. This book explains what's actually going on, in plain English, without the hype or the jargon.

AI is software that finds patterns and makes predictions. Once you see it that way, the headlines get less alarming, the tools get more useful, and you can decide for yourself where AI belongs in your life and your work.
backCover.highlightsLead: In this book you'll learn how to:
highlights: Spot the AI you already use every day
Understand what AI can and can't do, and why it sounds so sure of itself
Ask AI tools for what you actually want
Use AI at home and at work without handing over your judgement
